methods.label: Restrict one variable by divisibility
methods.explanation:
Because \(501\) and \(3x\) are divisible by \(3\), the equation forces \(5y\) to be divisible by \(3\). If \(y\) left remainder \(1\) or \(2\) upon division by \(3\), then \(5y\) would leave remainder \(2\) or \(1\), respectively. Thus \(y\) must be a multiple of \(3\).

Write \(y=3k\), where \(k\) is a positive integer. Substitution gives
\[
3x+15k=501,
\qquad x=167-5k.
\]
Now impose positivity. The condition \(y>0\) gives \(k\ge1\), while \(x\ge1\) gives \(5k\le166\). Since \(k\) is an integer, these conditions are exactly
\[
1\le k\le33.
\]
Every positive solution must arise this way. Conversely, each of these \(33\) integers produces a positive integer pair \((167-5k,3k)\) satisfying the equation. Different values of \(k\) give different values of \(y\), so no pair is counted twice. There are \(33\) solution-pairs, choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
